title: The attach operation, its right and the attach event name differ between the legacy story, the TSD and the Arch v5 event catalogue
source: RWB-E1-032 sections 10, 12 and 14; TSD P5 v2 T-A.1 API-P5-010 to API-P5-013 and T5.3; Arch v5 slides 16 and 42
description: The legacy story publishes POST /intake-items/{intakeItemId}/attach with the Documents right C and a 201 Document answer and writes DocumentStored. TSD P5 API-P5-013 declares POST /intake-items/{intakeItemId}/resolve with the right U and an IntakeResolution answer. Arch v5 slide 42 lists DocumentStored and DocumentFieldsExtracted for rwb-document, so the attach event name rwb.document.DocumentAttached.v1 is not in the catalogue. The field-level names of the four operations are absent, the exact path of the open-cases-by-account read is absent, and the name of the per-service database login is absent.
evidence: Legacy section 12: POST /intake-items/{intakeItemId}/attach ... Request IntakeAttachRequest ... Response 201 Document. TSD P5 v2 T-A.1 row API-P5-013 'POST /api/recovery/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/resolve | Documents U'. Arch v5 slide 42 row 16 'DocumentStored | rwb-document | rwb.document.events.v1'.
proposed: Publish /resolve as the attach operation with the Documents right C applied to the chosen case and the legacy 201 Document answer, declare rwb.document.DocumentAttached.v1 on rwb.document.events.v1, and have the event catalogue owner either add the name or confirm DocumentStored before the wave 1 release.

title: The intake-match contract baseline fixes shapes and paths the sources do not name at field level, and the plan's C list omits the two rwb-case reads
source: TSD P5 v2 T3.1, T3.2, T-A.2 and T5.3; FSD P5 A2.12; RWB-E1-032 section 12; plan metadata of RWB-P5-E1032-CON
description: The field names of IntakeItem, IntakeItemPage, IntakeAttachRequest and the not-found answer are not in any source beyond the legacy list; the exact path of the open-cases-by-account read is not stated; the idempotency window length is not stated; MSG-P4-001 and the not-found message text are not in the legacy section 14; and the plan lists only RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON as C dependencies while the baseline consumes two rwb-case case reads.
evidence: TSD P5 v2 T-A.2 API-P5-012 'Response: Binary' and API-P5-013 'Response: IntakeResolution' give no field list; legacy section 12 gives caseId, documentType and version only; plan slice RWB-P5-E1032-CON carries C ['RWB-P3-E1042-CON','RWB-P3-E1043-CON'].
proposed: The baseline fixes the four shapes as the smallest superset of the legacy list, declares the four consumed rows with their fakes and keeps every unnamed element behind the placeholder until the owner documents confirm them.

title: The compute, storage, hold-container and scanning capacity values of the intake-match path are not specified
source: Arch v5 slides 16, 38 and 44; TSD P5 v2 T7 NFR-004 and NFR-069; FSD P5 A2.7 AC-ALT-P5-007-01 and A2.18
description: The worker replica count, the request and limit set, the KEDA ceiling, the growth figure of document_text and its index budget, the clearing age of rwb-quarantine, the hold container capacity and the scan rate per hour are absent. The four-workers figure and the 500-page sample of the OCR module are test values and not sizing targets.
evidence: FSD P5 A2.7 AC-ALT-P5-007-01 '500 pages in 125 CLEAN intake items ... with 4 workers'; TSD P5 v2 NFR-069 'about 5.8 million documents and 2.8 TB by the end of 2031' gives the estate and no per-table figure; no source gives a replica count or a scan rate.
proposed: Provision the shape of each value now, set the numbers per environment from the SIT measurement of one business-hour window and the scan product's throughput, and record the agreed values in the environment files.

title: The Schedule window, the catch-up policy, the alert thresholds and the lag-alert identifier of the intake path are not specified
source: Arch v5 slide 44; FSD P5 AC-BG-P5-012-01; RWB-E1-032 section 12; NFR-068
description: The legacy story states every 15 minutes in business hours and Arch v5 slide 44 states every 15 minutes with no window, so the exact business-hours window, the overlap and catch-up policy, the run-failure threshold, the held-item age threshold, the KEDA threshold and the consumer-lag threshold are absent, and the lag alert has no message identifier in the source set.
evidence: RWB-E1-032 section 12 'Schedule | Every 15 minutes in business hours'; Arch v5 slide 44 'JOB-12 | Document intake | every 15 min | rwb-document | event + KEDA workers'; no source names a message ID for a lag alert.
proposed: Register the Schedule for the business-hours window with overlap policy skip and a catch-up of one run, hold every threshold as an environment value, and give the lag alert the placeholder until the Error and Message Standard names it.

title: The target retention and virus-scan surface of rwb-document, the scan attributes of an upload and the C row of the P3 case contract are not specified
source: TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1 (retention_rule DF-REF-116 to DF-REF-127, retention_action DF-DOC-091 to DF-DOC-095, document_intake DF-DOC-058 and DF-DOC-059) and T-A.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 41 and 44 (JOB-17 in rwb-document); legacy RWB-E1-041 sections 3, 4 and 12
description: The legacy story reaches the scan through the in-process MalwareScanService interface, loads the retention classes through a reference-load step whose table code is RETENTION_CLASS, and reads legal_hold through the P3 CaseDirectory interface; no source names the REST paths, the query parameters or the field sets of the scan request, the two scan-status reads, the two retention-rule reads or the three class-load operations. TSD P5 T-A.1 lists no scan endpoint and no retention admin endpoint. The two scan attributes sit on document_intake only, while an upload creates no intake item, so the story adds them to document as a design column. The plan gives RWB-P5-E1041-APP one C row (RWB-P3-E1043-CON) and none for the P3 case contract the hold is read through.
evidence: TSD P5 v2 T-A.1 endpoint inventory (API-P5-001 to API-P5-017) contains no scan and no retention-load endpoint; legacy RWB-E1-041 section 12 names the published interface MalwareScanService and the reference-load step without a request or response shape; split plan C list of RWB-P5-E1041-APP is [RWB-P3-E1043-CON]; FSD P5 v3 A2.17/A2.18 describe the run and the scan as steps, not as APIs
owner_role: Solution architect, with the P5 TechX squad
proposed: RWB-P5-E1041-CON publishes the eight operations with their paths, query parameters, field sets and statuses on /api/recovery/document/v1 before the wave-1 harness, and the split plan adds the C row for the P3 case contract or states that the hold read is consumed and faked by ruling.

title: No source names the retention and scan API of rwb-document, the class-load shape, the RetentionApplied event or the retention-class row shape the load writes
source: TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1, T3.2 and T-A.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 41, 42 and 44; legacy RWB-E1-041 sections 4, 8, 12 and 14; Ownership Map v1 (retention_rule, retention_action to P5)
description: The contract baseline must publish eight operations, five resources, one event and one record, and no source document fixes any of their names: the legacy story names two in-process jobs, one published interface and a reference-load step, TSD P5 lists no retention-admin, no rule-read and no scan endpoint, and the service catalogue names two events (DocumentStored, DocumentFieldsExtracted) so a retention event is a third. The legacy class template of table RETENTION_CLASS (class_code, period_months, end_action, table_version) is also not the retention_rule shape the Ownership Map gives to P5 (record_class, retention_months, age_basis_field, end_action, rule_version), and the plan gives the story an empty Contract dependencies list while two P3 reads are consumed.
evidence: TSD P5 v2 T-A.1 has no retention or scan endpoint; TSD P5 T5.3 lists DocumentStored and DocumentFieldsExtracted only; Legacy RWB-E1-041 section 12 gives the class table as RETENTION_CLASS with class_code and period_months; LDM v8 DF-REF-116 to DF-REF-127 give retention_rule with record_class, retention_months, age_basis_field and rule_version; split plan C list of RWB-P5-E1041-CON is empty
owner_role: Solution architect, with the P5 TechX squad and the platform event team
proposed: Freeze the eight operations, the five resources and the RetentionApplied schema in the rwb-document OpenAPI and AsyncAPI documents, record the event addition in the Kafka Topic and Event Catalog, and state that the RETENTION_CLASS template is accepted at the load and written to retention_rule.

title: OCR engine product, endpoint, engine version, capacity, intake request property names and the business-hours window are not named in the sources
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 049 OCR pipeline on the Workbench document hub v1.md sections 3, 4, 11, 12 and 13; TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1, T3.2 and T-A.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 41 and 44
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 12.1 REST operations provided; 12.6 Schedules; 13 Solution plan
description: The legacy story names the provider only as the OCR service run by Autonomous Ops under the service identity SY-OCR and gives the Schedule only as every 15 minutes in business hours, Asia/Bangkok. No source names the engine product, the engine version, the endpoint, the per-request page limit, the capacity or the exact business-hours window, and none gives the document_hub_parameter row load or the request property names of the intake submit. The APP file keeps every legacy value, treats the engine as the external X dependency RWB-P5-E1049-INF, and marks the missing elements with this row.
evidence: RWB-E1-049 section 3: The OCR service run by Autonomous Ops is reachable from SIT through the OcrClient adapter under the service identity SY-OCR; section 12: Every 15 minutes in business hours, Asia/Bangkok; TSD P5 T3.1 carries ocr_engine_version varchar(40) with no value.
proposed: Name the engine product, endpoint, engine version and page limit with the provider owner, and set the business-hours window and the four parameter rows as data at the wave 1 entry check.

title: The pipeline publishes a third event name on rwb.document.events.v1 while the architecture catalogue lists two events for rwb-document
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16 and 41 (rwb-document topic: DocumentStored, DocumentFieldsExtracted); RWB-P5-E2026-CON AC8 (a third event fails the absence test); RWB-E1-049 section 12 (Events published: None)
description: The OCR pipeline needs a completion signal so that the classify and extract steps start on the item rather than poll it. The architecture catalogue lists exactly DocumentStored and DocumentFieldsExtracted for rwb-document, and the generation baseline of the same service states that a third event fails its absence test. The contract baseline declares rwb.document.OcrCompleted.v1 with an eight-field payload and no personal data, and records the conflict here rather than adding the name silently.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 16: topic rwb.document.events.v1: DocumentStored, DocumentFieldsExtracted; slide 41 the same; RWB-E1-049 section 12 row Events published: None.
proposed: Add rwb.document.OcrCompleted.v1 to the service event catalogue and to the two-event count of RWB-P5-E2026-CON, or replace it with a status read by the classify and extract steps.

title: Field-level names of IntakeItem, OcrTextPage and IntakeStatus, the OCR status path and the not-found message ID are not specified
source: TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1, T3.2, T-A.1 and T-A.2; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 049 OCR pipeline on the Workbench document hub v1.md sections 11, 12 and 14
section: 11 Data; 12.1 REST operations provided; 12.5 Workflows and activities; 14 Validation and messages
description: TSD P5 T-A.1 names the intake item read with the response IntakeItem and gives no field list, and T3.1 gives the field IDs DF-DOC-045 to DF-DOC-090 without JSON property names. The legacy story gives no not-found message ID, no path segment for an OCR status read and no workflow payload. The contract baseline derives the property names from the field names, declares GET .../ocr-status, names the workflow input and output, and publishes all three for consumer sign-off.
evidence: TSD P5 T-A.1: API-P5-011 GET /intake-items/{intakeItemId}, Response IntakeItem, no field list; T3.1 field rows only; RWB-E1-049 section 14 lists MSG-P5-018 and MSG-P4-002 only.
proposed: Sign off the derived property names, the ocr-status path and the workflow payload with the four consumers at baseline review, and add the not-found message to the message catalogue.

title: OCR engine capacity, admission queue depth, per-page text size and container quota are not named in the sources
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 20, 38 and 46 (500 pages an hour; KEDA scales bursty OCR queues to zero); TSD P5 Document hub v2 T7 (NFR-004, NFR-069); RWB-E1-049 sections 3 and 4
description: The architecture gives a 500-pages-an-hour target and scale-to-zero for document OCR but no capacity figure for the engine, no admission queue depth, no bytes per page or per item and no container quota. The infrastructure story sizes the endpoint on the published target with headroom, binds the worker pool to the Temporal backlog with OCR_WORKERS = 4 per pod, and leaves the queue depth, the per-page size and the quota as environment values of the capacity review.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 46: OCR and document intake: bursts of uploads; 500 pages an hour; slide 20: KEDA Temporal scaler can scale bursty queues such as document OCR to zero; NFR-069: about 5.8 million documents and 2.8 TB by the end of 2031.
proposed: Set the capacity ceiling, the admission depth, the bytes per page and the container quota at the capacity review with the OCR provider owner.

title: The business-hours window, the deployment slot and the alert thresholds of the document intake pipeline are not specified
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 049 OCR pipeline on the Workbench document hub v1.md sections 12 and 13; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44 (JOB-12 every 15 min); RWB-PLT-E1056-OPS (alert thresholds assumed, DL11)
section: 12.6 Schedules; 13 Solution plan (alert mapping); 14 Validation and messages
description: The legacy story fixes the cadence and the zone of JOB-12 but not the business-hours window, and no source gives the failed-run threshold, the held-item age, the engine error-rate value or the deployment slot of the service. The operations story registers the Schedule from environment values with the legacy cadence and overlap SKIP, and treats the thresholds and the slot as provisional deployment values.
evidence: RWB-E1-049 section 12: Schedule Every 15 minutes in business hours, Asia/Bangkok; Architecture v5 slide 44: JOB-12 Document intake, every 15 min, rwb-document, event + KEDA workers; no threshold or slot appears in any source.
proposed: Set the business-hours window, the four alert thresholds and the deployment slot at the wave 1 entry check with the platform administrator.

title: The classify run is drawn as an rwb-agent child while the legacy story calls the P10 model gateway in process, and no source names the model provider, endpoint or model version
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16 (P5 IN: events AgentRunCompleted (classification); TMP Agent: child: classify / extract run) and slide 42 event 28; legacy RWB-E1-050 sections 3, 4 step 4 and 13 (ClassifierClient, ModelGatewayClassifier, rwb.dochub.classify.model-route, DL33)
description: The legacy story calls a classifier through the P10 model gateway with a route property set under DL33 and records classifier_version. Architecture v5 slide 16 draws the classify run as an agent child and lists AgentRunCompleted (classification) among the events rwb-document consumes, while the plan gives RWB-P5-E1050-APP no C row for rwb-agent or the agent contract. No source names the model provider, the endpoint route value, the model version string, the on-demand trigger of the evaluation runner or the container and account that hold the evaluation report.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 16 notes: 'rwb-document ... IN: ... events AgentRunCompleted (classification) ... TMP Agent: child: classify / extract run'; RWB-E1-050 section 3: 'The classifier model endpoint is set under DL33 and reachable through the P10 model gateway in SIT; its model version is known'; the plan C list of RWB-P5-E1050-APP is RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON only
owner_role: Solution architect with the TechX tech lead of rwb-document and the rwb-agent owner
proposed: Build the classifier as a service-internal capability behind ClassifierClient with a stub, a route property and no new dependency id; track the agent and model-gateway satellite as external work; confirm the provider, the endpoint and the model version string before the SIT evaluation, and add the C row to the plan then if the satellite stays

title: No source names a classification operation, path or field-level name, a 404 message identifier is absent, and a classification event would be a third event for rwb-document
source: TSD P5 v2 appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2 (API-P5-001 to API-P5-017, no classify operation); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 42 (events 16 and 17 only for rwb-document); RWB-P5-E2026-CON AC8 (exactly two events for rwb-document); legacy RWB-E1-050 section 12
description: The baseline declares POST /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/classify and GET /api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/classification because no source names a classification path, fixes the field names of ClassificationRequest, ClassificationResult and TypeCandidate as its own proposal, leaves the 404 not-found message identifier and text and the MSG-P4-001 text as placeholders, and declares rwb.document.DocumentClassified.v1 as a third event on the service topic. The service catalogue, the event and messaging document and the event count fixed by RWB-P5-E2026-CON must be amended in the same change.
evidence: TSD P5 appendix T-A.1 lists API-P5-001 to API-P5-017 and none is a classify operation; API-P5-011 to API-P5-014 read the intake item, its content, its resolution and the document review; Architecture v5 slide 42 lists only events 16 DocumentStored and 17 DocumentFieldsExtracted for rwb-document; RWB-P5-E2026-CON AC8: 'only rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1 and rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1 exist for rwb-document'
owner_role: Solution architect with the TechX contract owner of rwb-document
proposed: Declare the two operations on the service base and tag the baseline only after the architect confirms or renames them; settle the three resource field names with RWB-P5-E1050-APP, RWB-P5-E1032-APP and RWB-P5-E1054-APP; add DocumentClassified.v1 to the event catalogue and amend the event count and AC8 of RWB-P5-E2026-CON in the same change

title: The classifier artefact production and versioning, the evaluation report container, the alert thresholds and the deployment topology values are named by no source
source: Legacy RWB-E1-050 sections 13 and 16; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44 JOB-12; TSD P5 v2 T3.1; RWB-P5-E1050-CON and RWB-P5-E1050-APP
description: No source states how the classifier artefact is produced, versioned and promoted, which container and account hold evaluation/classification/{runDate}.json, what review-share, unknown-type-share and fallback thresholds the alerts use, or what replica counts, KEDA thresholds, probe timings and resource sizes the release carries. The story fixes only the pinning-and-rollback rule, the 162 of 180 gate, the names of the series and the rule that no number is hard-coded; every number stays a values entry.
evidence: RWB-E1-050 section 13 names only the property rwb.dochub.classify.model-route and the flag rwb.dochub.classify; Architecture v5 slide 44 gives JOB-12 'every 15 min, rwb-document, event + KEDA workers' and no artefact policy; TSD P5 v2 T3.1 gives classifier_version varchar(40) and no artefact version scheme; no source lists dashboard or alert thresholds
owner_role: DevOps engineer with the platform administrator and the data steward
proposed: Pin the classifier artefact by digest and promote it as one (chart, artefact) pair, roll back as one pair with no schema change, gate promotion on the 162 of 180 report, and take the alert shares, windows, replica counts, KEDA thresholds, probe timings and report container as values entries to be set at the SIT entry check

title: The extractor provider, model name and model version behind extraction_method MODEL are not named
source: RWB-E1-053 section 13 (ModelFieldExtractor calls the model through the P10 model gateway RWB-TE-013); Architecture v5 slides 16 and 41 (rwb-agent, Enterprise AI private endpoint INT-23); TSD P5 T3.1
section: 1 Story; 3 Preconditions; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 13 Solution plan
description: The legacy story names only the P10 model gateway (RWB-TE-013) as the model path. No source names the provider, the model, the model version, the route path or the answer shape of a field-extraction route, so the story fixes only the route name and the property rwb.document.extract.model-route.
evidence: RWB-E1-053 section 13 row ModelFieldExtractor: 'Calls the model through the P10 model gateway (RWB-TE-013) for extraction_method MODEL, with masked text as in RWB-E1-050.' Architecture v5 slide 16 P10 line names rwb-agent, schema rwb_agent, AgentRunCompleted and the Enterprise AI private endpoint, and names no model and no extraction route.
area: P5 Document hub / P10 agent contract
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-agent owner
proposed: Name the provider, the model, the model version and the field-extraction route in the rwb-agent contract baseline RWB-P10-TE013-CON, and keep the route a property of rwb-document with no model name in code.

title: No source names a REST operation or a path for running extraction, for its state read or for its fields read
source: TSD P5 T-A.1 endpoint inventory (API-P5-001 to API-P5-017, none for extraction); Architecture v5 slide 16 P5 IN line (POST /documents, GET /documents/{id}, GET /cases/{id}/documents, POST /documents/generate)
section: 3 Preconditions; 12.1 REST operations provided; 13 Solution plan
description: The legacy extraction is a job step plus an in-process FieldExtraction interface, so no REST operation exists in any source. The three operations of the target contract are the baseline's own choice and are published as the target shape of the two legacy methods.
evidence: TSD P5 T-A.1 lists API-P5-001 to API-P5-017 with no extract operation; Architecture v5 slide 16 P5 IN line lists four document operations and no extract operation; RWB-E1-053 section 12 publishes two Java methods only.
proposed: Publish the three operations on the document base, record them in the service API catalogue and treat the legacy Java interface as retired.

title: The review reason EXTRACTION_FAILED is not a value of LOV-INTAKE-REVIEW
source: RWB-E1-053 exception X4 and AC8; TSD P5 T3.2 LOV-INTAKE-REVIEW (RESCAN, UNREADABLE_FILE, LOW_CONFIDENCE, MODEL_UNAVAILABLE, UNKNOWN_TYPE)
section: 5 Exception paths X4; 8 Business rules BR7; 9 State transitions; 14 Validation and messages
description: The legacy story sets review_reason EXTRACTION_FAILED when the extractor does not answer on every attempt. TSD P5 T3.2 has no such value, and the nearest value MODEL_UNAVAILABLE is the classification fallback value of RWB-E1-050, so the two conditions would be indistinguishable in the review queue.
evidence: RWB-E1-053 X4 'extract_status FAILED; review_reason EXTRACTION_FAILED' and AC8; TSD P5 T3.2 row LOV-INTAKE-REVIEW lists five values and no EXTRACTION_FAILED.
owner_role: Data steward with the P5 business analyst
proposed: Extend LOV-INTAKE-REVIEW with EXTRACTION_FAILED in the next approved list load, keep MODEL_UNAVAILABLE for the classification fallback and change no code.

title: No source fixes the field-level names of ExtractionRequest, ExtractedField and FieldSet, the extract operation paths or the event payload
source: RWB-E1-053 section 12 (job step input, the two FieldExtraction methods, event payload in prose); TSD P5 T3.1 document_field, document_intake, document_type columns; TSD P5 T5.3 events
section: 2 Business rationale; 11 Data; 12.1 REST operations provided; 12.3 Events published
description: The sources name two Java methods, a payload in prose and the document_field columns. They fix no resource name, no property set, no path and no event property list; this baseline fixes them and the consumers build against them, so a later rename is a breaking change of major version 1.
evidence: RWB-E1-053 section 12: 'List<ExtractedField> fieldsForIntake(UUID intakeId); // fieldName, value, extractedValue, confidence, state, extractorVersion, personal' and 'payload documentId, field names and confidence; no values'.
proposed: Adopt the shapes and the payload of this baseline as published version 1, allow additive change only inside major version 1, and align the API catalogue and the AsyncAPI fragment.

title: The field-extraction route of the rwb-agent contract, its answer field names and its model version are not named
source: RWB-E1-053 section 13; Architecture v5 slide 16 P10 contract line (REST GET /agent-runs/{id}; GET/POST /agent-policies)
section: 2 Business rationale; 5 Exception paths X7; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.8 Contract fakes
description: rwb-agent publishes an agent-run read and a policy admin surface, not an extraction route. The consumed contract is therefore named without a path, its answer names are fixed by this baseline and its fake, and the drift test holds the two together.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 16 P10 OUT line lists REST GET /agent-runs/{id} and GET/POST /agent-policies only; RWB-E1-053 section 13 names the P10 model gateway with no route.
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-agent owner
proposed: Add the field-extraction route with the typed answer of AC8 to RWB-P10-TE013-CON and publish it with its WireMock and the drift test.
